narrative: OMX30 opens into a globally bullish session with US equity strength (+2.35% S&P, +2.74% NASDAQ) and Asian outperformance (Nikkei +2.87%) driving +1.41% correlation bias. Domestically, the index sits +5.3% above its 200-MA in confirmed bull trend (ADX 35.5), MACD above signal, but Stochastic K=94.3 and %B=0.92 flash overbought extremes—classic setup for intra-day pullback. The 52-week level sits dead flat, and we're pinned at the upper Bollinger band. Key headwind: US 10Y +169bp spike (+4.946%) pressures tech DCF multiples (NASDAQ correlation +0.49), while oil -3.38% removes input-cost inflation pressure. Banks benefit from wider NIM; exporters supported by weak USD/SEK.
morningBrief: OMX30 expected to gap up +0.6–1.0% on global risk appetite, but watch for profit-taking once we hit 3135–3145 resistance zone (50-MA × Stochastic overbought). Strong ADX (35.5) confirms trend integrity, but RSI 62.64 + Stochastic extremes (K=94.3, D=78.7) signal mean reversion vulnerability—scalp shorts if we break 3150. Atlas Copco, Volvo, Ericsson should lead on USD/SEK tailwind; avoid H&M (EUR/SEK headwind). Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) ride NIM expansion; tech/software (Hexagon, Sinch) under pressure from yield spike. Key data point: US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET—expect volatility if surprise weak. Support holds at 3085 (lower BB); break below threatens 3050 (200-MA cushion).
